### Problem: Permutation Swap {#sec-idx-p3-permswap}

::: {.p-statement}
You are given an **unsorted** permutation $p_1, \ldots, p_n$. You choose one integer $k \ge 1$ and may then perform any number of operations, each swapping $p_i$ and $p_j$ with $i - j = k$. Find the **largest** $k$ for which the permutation can be sorted. Constraints: $t \le 10^4$, $2 \le n \le 10^5$, sum of $n$ at most $2 \cdot 10^5$. Samples: $[3, 1, 2] \to 1$; $[3, 4, 1, 2] \to 2$; $[4, 2, 6, 7, 5, 3, 1] \to 3$; $[1, 6, 7, 4, 9, 2, 3, 8, 5] \to 4$; $[1, 5, 3, 4, 2, 6] \to 3$; $[3, 10, 5, 2, 9, 6, 7, 8, 1, 4] \to 2$; $[1, 11, 6, 4, 8, 3, 7, 5, 9, 10, 2] \to 3$.

Source: [CF 1828B · Permutation Swap](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1828/B){.solved rating="900"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
A swap at distance $k$ never changes an element's position modulo $k$, and inside one residue class any arrangement is reachable. So $k$ works iff every value $p_i$ already sits in the class of its home $p_i$: $k \mid |p_i - i|$ for all $i$. The largest such $k$ is $\gcd_i |p_i - i|$.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Test each $k$.** For $k = n - 1, n - 2, \ldots, 1$, split the positions into the classes $r, r + k, r + 2k, \ldots$ and check that each class holds exactly the values whose homes are in it. Return the first $k$ that passes ($k = 1$ always does). With sorting per class, $O(n^2 \log n)$: the oracle.
2. **Running gcd.** $g \leftarrow 0$; for each 1-based $i$, $g \leftarrow \gcd(g, |p_i - i|)$. Return $g$. $O(n \log n)$.

**Why the test in step 1 is exact.** Necessity: a distance-$k$ swap moves an element between positions $j$ and $j + k$, which have the same residue mod $k$, so an element can never leave its class; the value $v$ must end at position $v$, so $v$ must start in the class of $v$. Sufficiency: within one class, swapping neighbours of the class (positions $j$ and $j + k$) is adjacent swapping on that class, which can sort it, as in bubble sort. Hence $k$ works iff $p_i \equiv i \pmod k$ for every $i$, i.e. $k$ divides every displacement, i.e. $k \mid g$. Every divisor of $g$ works, and the largest is $g$ itself. The permutation is unsorted, so some displacement is non-zero and $g \ge 1$.

**Worked trace.** $p = [4, 2, 6, 7, 5, 3, 1]$: the displacements $|p_i - i|$ are $[3, 0, 3, 3, 0, 3, 6]$, and their gcd is $3$. With $k = 3$ the classes are positions $\{1, 4, 7\}$ holding $\{4, 7, 1\}$, $\{2, 5\}$ holding $\{2, 5\}$, and $\{3, 6\}$ holding $\{6, 3\}$: each holds exactly its own homes.
:::

::: {#fig-idx-p3-permswap}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    perm = [4, 2, 6, 7, 5, 3, 1]
    k = 3
    cls = ["indigo", "green", "amber"]
    disp = [abs(v - i) for i, v in enumerate(perm, 1)]
    assert reduce(gcd, disp) == k
    V.array(ax, p, perm, label="p", colors={i: cls[i % k] for i in range(7)})
    V.array(ax, p, disp, y=-2.6, label="|p_i - i|", index=False,
            colors={i: cls[i % k] for i in range(7)}, note="gcd = 3")
V.show(draw)
```

The third sample, coloured by position modulo $3$. Every value sits in the colour class of its home (value $v$ belongs at 1-based position $v$), and every displacement is a multiple of $3$, so $k = 3$ sorts it and no larger $k$ divides $6$ and $3$ at once.

:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

#### Test each k

::: {.form-next}
For each candidate $k$ from large to small, compare each residue class's values with its home positions. The first $k$ that passes is the answer. Quadratic: the oracle for the gcd.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("permswap", "chains")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

##### Python

```{python}
def permswap_brute(p):
    n = len(p)
    for k in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
        if all(sorted(p[i] for i in range(r, n, k)) == [i + 1 for i in range(r, n, k)]
               for r in range(k)):
            return k
    return 1


assert permswap_brute([3, 1, 2]) == 1
assert permswap_brute([4, 2, 6, 7, 5, 3, 1]) == 3              # the board sample
```

##### C++

```cpp
int permswapBrute(const vector<int>& p) {
    int n = (int)p.size();
    for (int k = n - 1; k >= 1; k--) {
        bool ok = true;
        for (int r = 0; r < k && ok; r++) {
            vector<int> vals, homes;
            for (int i = r; i < n; i += k) { vals.push_back(p[i]); homes.push_back(i + 1); }
            sort(vals.begin(), vals.end());
            ok = vals == homes;
        }
        if (ok) return k;
    }
    return 1;
}
```

:::

#### Running gcd

::: {.form-next}
The test "every class holds its own homes" is the same as "$k$ divides every displacement", so the best $k$ is the gcd of the displacements. One pass, no classes. Zero displacements are harmless, since $\gcd(g, 0) = g$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("permswap", "gcd")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

##### Python

```{python}
def permswap(p):
    g = 0
    for i, v in enumerate(p, 1):
        g = gcd(g, abs(v - i))
    return g


samples = ([3, 1, 2], [3, 4, 1, 2], [4, 2, 6, 7, 5, 3, 1], [1, 6, 7, 4, 9, 2, 3, 8, 5],
           [1, 5, 3, 4, 2, 6], [3, 10, 5, 2, 9, 6, 7, 8, 1, 4], [1, 11, 6, 4, 8, 3, 7, 5, 9, 10, 2])
assert [permswap(p) for p in samples] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 3]
assert permswap([4, 2, 6, 7, 5, 3, 1]) == 3                    # the board sample
for _ in range(300):
    n = random.randint(2, 9)
    q = random.sample(range(1, n + 1), n)
    if q == sorted(q):                   # the input is promised unsorted
        continue
    assert permswap(q) == permswap_brute(q), q
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int gcdInt(int a, int b) {                // own gcd: std::gcd needs C++17 and <numeric>
    while (b) { int t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
    return a;
}

int main() {
    int t;
    scanf("%d", &t);
    while (t--) {
        int n;
        scanf("%d", &n);
        int g = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            int v;
            scanf("%d", &v);
            g = gcdInt(g, abs(v - i));
        }
        printf("%d\n", g);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Test each k:** $O(n^2 \log n)$ time (for each $k$, sort the classes), $O(n)$ space. **Running gcd:** $O(n \log n)$ time (each Euclid step is $O(\log n)$), $O(1)$ extra.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- One adjacent pair swapped, $[2, 1]$: displacements $[1, 1]$, answer $1$.
- The identity is excluded by the statement; it would give $\gcd = 0$, and "any $k$" would work.
- The displacement $|p_i - i|$ is the same for 0-based or 1-based indexing *as long as both value and index use the same base*. Mixing a 0-based index with a 1-based value shifts every displacement by one.
- The answer is the largest valid $k$, which can exceed the distance used to scramble the array: if every displacement is $6$ or $12$, the answer is $6$, not $1$ or $2$.
:::
